measurement.build_host: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu (GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest) — the `embedded` CI job is the gate and the authority for `measured_resident`/`resident_ram_max`/`measured_flash` since #927; the pinned host below is what the per-symbol itemization in `_resident_note` was diffed on (it links 8 B less resident and a different flash figure, neither of which is gated).
measurement.capacity_profile: LM20 (nRF54LM20-DK, 512 KiB SRAM; 500 KiB M33 carve; default = all-features/ble + the unconditional USB device plane; SDC size measured on glass 2026-07-24)

default.features: default (= all-features: map + router + BLE + USB device plane, LS021/FLPR, real sensors)
default._resident_note: 439,040 → 440,960 B (+1,920) for the volume-set FAT handle budget (#1026, epic #1016 P3b). `OBCA_Spec.md` §5 makes one logical map 1..32 physical files, and the epic's device-cost review requires a mounted set to hold **every** shard's handle open for the mount lifetime — re-opening per query would put a FAT directory walk in the render loop. `sd::SD_MAX_FILES` therefore goes 6 → 16: the 8 handles a DACH-shaped set needs (core + coarse + ~6 geometry) plus the unchanged 5-handle mid-ride peak documented above `SdSpi`, plus margin. **The whole increase is that one constant, and it costs 3× what the array does.** The fork's `FileInfo` (`filesystem/files.rs`) is `RawFile` 4 · `RawVolume` 4 · `current_cluster` 8 · `current_offset` 4 · `Mode` 1 · `DirEntry` 40 · `dirty` 1 = 64 B at align 4 on thumbv8m, held in `VolumeManager`'s `heapless::Vec<FileInfo, SD_MAX_FILES>`; ten more slots is 640 B per resident `VolumeManager`, and the image links **three**. Itemized by symbol diff against the identical tree with the constant back at 6: `__embassy_main::POOL` 31,312 → 32,592 (+1,280 — *two* copies of `Storage` inside main's async frame, because an async frame allocates every local at entry, the same #270 trap that put `MAP_EXTENTS` in its own `.bss` slot rather than inside `Storage`) and `SHARED_STORE` 5,728 → 6,368 (+640 — the copy that actually lives for the session). Nothing else moved: the same tree with `SD_MAX_FILES = 6` links exactly 439,040 B, so the rest of #1026 — the `MapSummary` growth for sets, `set_identity`, `delete_set`, the `MapChoice::set` field — costs **zero** resident bytes, and the compile-time allocation table is unchanged in all 23 entries. Poll frame unmoved at 9,728 B. Figures are **CI's** (the `embedded` job is the gate); this is a case where the pinned local host links the *identical* 440,960 B, and CI's `default` and `ble` legs agree byte for byte (run 30589233369: 440,960 B linked resident, flash 1,218,184 B on both legs), which is where `measured_flash` below comes from. Previously: 438,912 → 439,040 B (+128) for the OBCM v11 chunk-offset table (#1009), stacked on the #889 staging buffer below — the two are independent. The whole increase is one field, counted twice: `obc_reader::Lod` gained `chunk_bytes_total: usize` (the LOD's total chunk bytes, `offsets[Chunk Count]`, kept resident so a per-chunk fetch bounds its offset pair without a second read), and the reader holds `Vec<Lod, 16>` — so 4 B × 16 slots = 64 B per `MapTables`, of which the image has two: the static `MAP_TABLES` (4,060 → 4,124, see `compile_time_allocations`) and the copy inside the embassy task pool future. Measured on the merge of #1014 into this branch: 439,040 B, i.e. exactly the +128 it linked against the pre-#1014 base, so the offset table costs the same either side of that merge. Both figures are confirmed against this merge's own `embedded` run (30522203604): 439,040 B linked resident and flash 1,209,608 B, identical on the `default` and `ble` legs, and `measured_flash` below is taken from that log (local hosts link a different flash figure; flash is not gated for board profiles). The v11 offset table itself is *file* bytes, not resident ones, and buys back ~2.3× on every map. Poll frame unmoved at 9,728 B. Previously: 422,504 → 438,912 B (+16,408) for the map-upload staging buffer (#889). Figures are **CI's** (the `embedded` job is the gate); this increase is the rare case where the pinned local host links the **identical** 438,912 B and CI's `default` and `ble` legs agree byte for byte (run 30520773708). The increase is one named allocation plus its future: `usb_named` 2,652 → 19,036 (+16,384) is `usb::STAGE_LEN`, a 16 KiB `.bss` buffer the USB data plane fills from the bulk endpoint and drains to the card a batch at a time. It exists because the embedded-sdmmc fork can only issue an ACMD23+CMD25 multi-block write for what one `VolumeManager::write` hands it, and the plane previously handed it one 512 B packet at a time — 2,458 µs/block against 478 at 64-block batches (`sd_bench` `wr-*`, on glass). The remaining +24 B is the USB data-plane task's `TaskStorage`: `run_upload`'s future gained one `link::stage::Stage` local (a `&mut [u8]` fat pointer plus two `usize` counters), and embassy sizes task storage from the future. 16 KiB and not 32: it takes ~94% of the batching win, and the second 16 KiB would halve the margin between the ~72 KiB residual stack and the 35,808 B measured deep-ride peak — this is the crate where async frames overflow silently. Poll frame unmoved at 9,728 B. Previously: 422,208 → 422,504 B (+296) for the `Next: <category>` stat fields' per-category cache (#951, epic #946, U5). Figures are **CI's** (the `embedded` job is the gate and runs floating stable); the pinned local host links 8 B less resident (422,496 measured here) and a different flash figure, neither of which is gated — Both resident figures were **confirmed against the `embedded` job** (run 30371199831: 422,504 B linked resident, `app` 136,504 B, identical on the `default` and `ble` legs), and `measured_flash` below is taken from the same log. The whole increase is one named allocation: `app` 136,208 → 136,504 (+296), i.e. `size_of::<App>()`. It is the new `UiRuntime::next_ahead` (`NextAhead`): six cache lines of `Option<NextPoi { u32, String<24> }>` + an `Option<u32>` take anchor, plus the scheduler's request/turn/route fields. Held once in `App` for the same #425 reason as `poi_scratch` and `corridor_scratch` — a `Screen` variant is a slot in a `.bss` union, so inline it would multiply across all 10 stack slots. It buys the stat tiles their answer *without* a second 16-slot corridor buffer: the snapshot is distilled to one `(dist_along_m, name)` per category and the shared `CorridorScratch` is reused as-is. Poll frame unmoved at 9,728 B. Previously: 422,080 → 422,208 B (+128) and flash 1,190,108 → 1,189,884 for the OBCR v3 waypoint record (#947). Figures are **CI's** (the `embedded` job is the gate and runs floating stable); the pinned local host links 8 B less resident and a different flash figure, neither of which is gated. The whole increase is one named allocation: `app` 136,080 → 136,208 — the resident `Waypoints` table's 32 × `WptEntry` at +4 B each, the entry having gained `category: Option<PoiCategory>` (1 B, niche-packed) and `lateral_offset_m: i16`, which fit in the record's existing tail padding. Nothing else moved, and flash *fell* 224 B (the reader lost its two-version branches). Poll frame unmoved at 9,728 B. Previously: 421,224 → 422,080 B (+856) and flash 1,185,668 → 1,190,108 for the route-corridor POI snapshot (#948, epic #946). Figures are **CI's** (the `embedded` job is the gate and runs floating stable); the pinned local host links 8 B less resident, the usual layout difference, and a different flash figure — neither is gated. The whole increase is **one named allocation**: `app` 135,224 → 136,080 B (+856), i.e. `size_of::<App>()`. Nothing else moved — the delta and the `app` delta are the same 856 bytes. It is the new `UiRuntime::corridor_scratch` (`CorridorScratch`): a 16-slot `heapless::Vec<CorridorPoi>` (16 × 52 B = 832) plus its `want`/`taken_for` snapshot keys. Held once in `App` **by design**, exactly like `poi_scratch` before it — inline in the `Screen` union it would multiply across all 10 stack slots (~8.6 KB) instead of costing the buffer once (issue #425). Poll frame unmoved at 9,728 B.

floating_stable_observation._comment: Hand-recorded snapshot of what CI's floating-stable toolchain links; nothing regenerates it. SUPERSEDED as of #927: the profile figures above are now taken from CI directly (run 30306462532), so this block no longer carries the only CI datapoint. Kept for the trend it records — CI at 5eb3e72e linked 421,128, at 9bb7adf8 421,176, and with #927 421,224 — and for the point it was written to make: floating stable links the same resident set and the same poll frame as the pinned toolchain, differing only in flash.
